significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, across recursive distillation generations, trait strength follows amplification, extinction, or directional-drift regimes governed by measurable "per-generation transfer gain" and "stability of the underlying steering direction," thereby predicting later-generation trajectories and regime changes. This establishes a behavioral phenomenon plus a partial dynamical mechanism, although the statements that gain above one amplifies and gain below one decays are partly definitional, and the broad alternatives "amplify, decay, and drift" weaken determinacy; the valuable part is whether early gain and direction stability consistently predict unseen generations and whether traits can "emerge or entrench ... without ever being explicitly present in any single dataset." A negative result would meaningfully rule out the proposed low-dimensional gain-and-direction account of recursive transmission, relevant alongside Shumailov et al.'s Nature 2024 finding of distributional collapse under recursive synthetic-data training, rather than merely failing to locate one steering direction. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: subliminal learning alone would not imply phase thresholds, multigeneration prediction, or spontaneous entrenchment, so the score rests on claim-specific structure rather than the topic's general importance.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly named as "per-generation transfer gain g," "amplification/extinction thresholds," and "steering-vector cosine drift per generation." These can provide limited ex-ante lead time: after estimating gain and stability in early generations, an auditor could forecast accumulation or extinction before completing a longer recursive training chain, although the claim does not provide a pre-training screen and some drift characterization remains post hoc. After model-specific re-extraction, the claimed gain-to-trajectory and stability-to-drift relations would still predict what later generations should do, while the numerical thresholds themselves would require recalibration; the hypothesis ranges across traits and recursive distillation settings, with plausible uptake by researchers and practitioners auditing or gating synthetic-data pipelines. The topic-substitution check passes because the assigned topic alone supplies neither these measurable handles nor their forward-looking coupling, but the absence of a fully model-independent design rule keeps reach below the top bands.
